statement.p:
State the geometric effect of the matrix transformation defined by
\left[\begin{array}{rr} 3 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp -1 \\ \end{array}\right] .

solution.p: This matrix transformation stretches vectors by a factor of 3 in the horizontal direction and flips vectors vertically.

statement.p:
Suppose that A is a 2\times 2 matrix and that \vvec_1 and \vvec_2 are vectors such that
A\vvec_1 = 3 \vvec_1, \qquad A\vvec_2 = -\vvec_2 . Use the linearity of matrix multiplication to express the following vectors in terms of \vvec_1 and \vvec_2.
A(4\vvec_1).
A(\vvec_1 + \vvec_2).
A(4\vvec_1 -3\vvec_2).
A^2\vvec_1.
A^2(4\vvec_1 - 3\vvec_2).
A^4\vvec_1.

solution.p:
Applying linearity, we see that
A(4\vvec_1) = 4A\vvec_1 = 12\vvec_1.
A(\vvec_1+\vvec_2) = A\vvec_1 + A\vvec_2 = 3\vvec_1 - \vvec_2.
A(4\vvec_1-3\vvec_2) = 4A\vvec_1 -3A\vvec_2 = 12\vvec_1 + 3\vvec_2.
A^2\vvec_1 = A(3\vvec_1) = 9\vvec_1.
A^2(4\vvec_1-3\vvec_2) = A(12\vvec_1 +3\vvec_2) = 36\vvec_1 - 3\vvec_2.
A^4\vvec_1 = 3^4\vvec_1 = 81\vvec_1.
